title: content/shop/shop.json
description: The loc keys the run Shop screen (S08) renders. What is fixed here is that the screen heads the tile, prices and captions four buy slots, offers a restock and a departure, and carries one status line per state the read and a submission can be in. Every value is a loc key, so the content build resolves it against every locale file: a key this document names but a locale does not carry fails the build, and a locale string this document stops naming fails it as an orphan. additionalProperties is false on every object so the absences are enforced rather than merely observed. ⚠️ THIS SCHEMA WAS ONCE ABOUT ITS ABSENCES: it had no member for a buy slot, a price, a stock line or a refresh control, because a run carried no offer state and the rules layer refused every purchase. The run-tiles pass of 2026-08-20 (16 D38) built the visit — an offer position, a purchase mask and a refresh count — so all four slots are real, priced and buyable, and SHOP_LEAVE is what clears the tile. What is STILL absent is a per-item name: a slot is captioned by the POOL it drew from, because the perk, consumable and run-buff catalogues already name their own rows and a second document claiming those keys would be free to drift out of step with the pools it describes. These keys are the RUN shop's and are three segments deep; the four-segment staple and daily keys already in the locales belong to the meta shop's offer catalogue and are a different screen's.

locKey.description: loc.<domain>.<id>.<field>, lowercase, dot-separated, snake_case segments — the same shape schema/loc.schema.json governs the locale files by.

name.description: The screen's own heading, so a player can tell which tile they are standing on.

action.description: 🔒 The three controls this screen has. `leave` is SHOP_LEAVE, the tile's clearing step and the ONLY way off it — a run whose leave caption went missing is a run standing on a tile it cannot read its way off. `buy` and `refresh` are the two that used to be absent, and their absence used to be this schema's whole point: the run row now carries a visit, an offer position and a refresh count, so both are controls whose press has a real outcome.

label.description: 🔒 The four slot names and the four words a slot is captioned with. A slot that cannot be pressed carries its reason IN WORDS — sold, too dear, nothing left in this pool — because three different refusals greyed out identically leave a player unable to tell 'you already have this' from 'you cannot afford this'. `gold` heads the run-local total the prices are against.

block.description: The one permanent sentence left: a visit whose free refresh and the run's ad refreshes are all spent says so, rather than hiding the control and leaving the player to infer why.

status.description: One line per state the read can be in, plus the answers a submission can come back with. `notAtAShop` is separated from `runMissing` because a screen opened on the wrong tile is not a run that has gone; `offerUnavailable` from both, because a run standing at a stocked shop whose CONTENT could not be read is a different fact again, and the screen keeps its departure through it; `refused` and `hostUnavailable` because a refusal is an answer about the game and a fault is the game not answering; and `unaffordable` from `refused`, because it is the one refusal the player can act on.
